notes.architecture: Electron desktop app (presentation software for churches). src/electron = main process: IPC handlers (IPC/responsesMain.ts), output windows/capture (output/), data and storage (data/), local servers, NDI/Blackmagic/streaming. src/frontend = Svelte 4 renderer: global stores in stores.ts, UI in components/, importers in converters/. src/server = small Svelte web apps (remote, stage, controller, cam) served on the LAN. src/types = shared types, including the IPC enums and payload maps.
conventions: New IPC message: add the enum and payload type in src/types/IPC/Main.ts or ToMain.ts, then the handler in src/electron/IPC/responsesMain.ts or src/frontend/IPC/responsesMain.ts
Unit tests are *.test.ts next to the source, run by vitest with config/testing/vitest.config.ts; mock ../IPC/main and ../utils/files, use os.tmpdir() for files
Output windows are separate renderers: frontend stores are not shared with them unless explicitly sent
Platform-specific code branches on isWindows/isMac/isLinux exported from src/electron/index.ts
UI strings live in public/lang/en.json (translateText / <T id>)
Prettier config is config/formatting/.prettierrc.yaml; format and svelte-check have a pre-existing backlog, compare before/after instead of expecting zero
risks: Native modules (NDI, Blackmagic, better-sqlite3, opus) must be built on the target OS; installers built from WSL/Linux break on Windows
Windows/macOS-only code (PowerPoint COM bridge in src/electron/output/ppt/) cannot run under WSL; test on a real Windows build
User data lives in Documents/FreeShow (shows, projects, backups); changes to data formats need migration and must not lose data
Remote/stage/controller servers are reachable on the LAN; keep their auth and inputs validated
